commits.subject: 📝 Record the merge and the plan for 0.11.0

why: PR #5 passed CI on every platform, and we're releasing on 2026-11-03 without the sprint the roadmap asks for, so the roadmap should say both.

commits.subject: 💚 Make the memory and MCP tests pass on Windows

why: Windows CI failed five tests that assumed POSIX behaviour: git there can't print dates this far out, a command line stops at 32 KB, and an absolute POSIX path gets a different error. Each commit still stays in memory and each path still errors, so only the tests change.

commits.subject: 💚 Keep the huge-body test within argument limits

why: the fixture passes the body with git commit -m, and Linux refuses a single argument over 128 KB, so the test failed on Ubuntu with E2BIG.

commits.subject: 🔒 Redact the whole of a long email address

why: the 64-character cap on the local part left the start of a longer address in the text sent to Jev.
constraint: the pattern has to stay linear on a long run of word characters, so a lookbehind stops a match starting partway through a run.

commits.subject: 📝 Drop the docs for foreign entries and --no-verify

why: the readme and plan said memory sync skips the pre-push hook and that writes keep entries chamoji doesn't read; both are gone, and the plan's test name for purge is current.

commits.subject: ⏪ Stop carrying foreign tree entries, and let the pre-push hook run

why: the re-review reproduced three breaks from carrying foreign entries (a pushed gitlink makes mktree die and blocks every write including purge, a blobless clone can't write, a behind clone can revert a newer edit), and the feature was speculative; a pre-push hook can be a user's policy check, so skipping it was not ours to decide.
constraint: older clients drop what they don't know, so the memory ref's layout is fixed until a new format gets its own ref or a version bump.
followUp: a future memory format needs its own ref or a version bump, because released clients drop paths and modes they don't know.

commits.subject: 📝 Document the final review fixes for project memory

why: the fixes changed what the commands print and do, and the docs still told people to run a raw force-push after a purge.

commits.subject: 🐛 Fix the issues found in the final review of project memory

why: a whole-branch review found that following the printed purge step could erase a teammate's unsynced memory from origin, that one huge commit could stall --ai search for minutes, and that an older chamoji would strip a newer one's entries from the shared ref.
constraint: the memory ref is untrusted, so foreign tree entries are rebuilt only when their names are safe and their depth is bounded, and a larger mode and id wins a clash so every clone settles on one tree.
gotcha: the card is read from below the first paragraph of a message, because git counts that whole paragraph as the subject, so git commit -m with a Why line on the second line has no card.
followUp: run the rerank against the real TypeSafe API, and check the .mcp.json that init --agents writes on native Windows.

commits.subject: 📝 Correct the project memory docs after review

why: a reviewer checked the docs against the code and found claims that were wrong or unsupported, and a README that overstates what is sent or searched misleads the people it is meant to protect.
gotcha: memory search --ai and mcp --ai skip a tracked .env file, so the key sources differ from changelog --ai's.

commits.subject: 📝 Document project memory and record milestone 7

why: the milestone is built, and a reader needs to know what it does, what it sends, what was checked against real clients and what was not.
constraint: Milestone 7 is not done until a sprint of real use, so the status stays "Built, release pending" and ws ship and memory sync wait for release.
gotcha: fish, pwsh, Windows and a real push of the memory ref to GitHub are not verified, and the docs say so.
followUp: run the sprint of real use on this repo, then ws ship, memory sync and release.

commits.subject: 🔒 Bound the why body, lock down temp files, stop inviting the opt-out

why: Real Claude Code took the CHAMOJI_NO_CARD opt-out on its first denial because the old text invited it, and the final security review asked for the body bound and the 0600 temp file.
constraint: A new file still gets the default permissions (0666 minus the umask), so only the temp file starts at 0600.
gotcha: The temp file's 0600 creation mode has no direct test, since it only exists between the write and the chmod; the tests cover the final modes.

commits.subject: 🐛 Keep the agent hook from blocking commits and from changing shared files

why: a committed hook command that exits 2 on a chamoji without agent-hook blocks every commit in the repo, and a rewrite that silently changes a value or half-writes a shared file costs the team more than the setup saves
constraint: Claude Code reads exit 2 as a block, so both command forms end in `|| true`; a denial is JSON on stdout with exit 0 and still gets through
gotcha: decideCommit still skips shell keywords, so `if true; then git commit -m x; fi` is allowed; a table test pins that
the number check compares each number's digits before and after JSON.parse and stringify, so 1.50 and 1E2 are fine and 12345678901234567890 is refused

commits.subject: ✨ Make AI agents write an intent card when they commit

why: a denial reaches the agent while it can still write the card, whereas context added after the commit arrives too late to change it
constraint: the hook must print only the decision JSON or nothing and always exit 0, so a broken hook never stops the agent's work
.mcp.json and .claude/settings.json are shared files, so init merges into them, keeps their key order and indent, and refuses a corrupt file or a symlink without touching either
gotcha: decideCommit reads free-form shell text with a small quote and heredoc scanner, not a shell parser, so aliases, variables and sh -c are not seen
the hook command is chosen once, by whether chamoji is on PATH when init runs, and a committed file then carries that choice to teammates
followUp: try the hook with real Claude Code, which the controller runs after all tasks

commits.subject: 🔒 Bound and sanitize what chamoji mcp sends to the model

why: commits and memory are written by other people, so the server must not hand a model unbounded text, other people's addresses, or a file a clone pointed it at
constraint: reads of the workstreams file now throw WorkstreamError for a symlink, so ws and the hook see that error where they used to follow the link
gotcha: JSON.stringify leaves U+2028 and U+2029 raw, which a client that splits on Unicode line separators would cut a reply at

commits.subject: ✨ Serve project memory to AI agents with chamoji mcp

why: an agent editing a line should be able to ask why it is the way it is, and get the card its author wrote
constraint: no MCP SDK; it would double chamoji's install for five methods
gotcha: tool names and methods go through a Map or a switch, so "constructor" is unknown rather than found on Object.prototype
--ai must be skipped by the commit classifier in run.ts, or a missing key would exit 1 before the server starts
followUp: try it with the real Claude Code client (claude mcp add)

commits.subject: 🔒 Keep commit text and tracked env files out of the memory rerank

why: a tracked .env could name another account's key and receive the query and history text, and commit text in the instructions could steer the ranking
constraint: changelog `--ai` keeps reading a tracked env file as before
gotcha: the TypeSafe docs don't spell out how a question refers to nested state, so the `candidates[i]` wording follows the commit classifier's `commits[i]`

commits.subject: ✨ Search project memory with BM25 and an optional Jev rerank

why: a card nobody can find doesn't help the next person, and search has to work offline with no key so Jev can only ever reorder what BM25 already found
constraint: term lookups use a Map, because commit text is other people's and a word like `constructor` or `__proto__` must be an ordinary term
the index file is validated on load and rebuilt, never trusted, and a search still runs when it can't be saved
gotcha: `--ai` on `memory` no longer builds the changelog classifier, so `memory search --ai` without a key exits 2 like other misuse
followUp: tokenize splits on anything that isn't a letter or number as specified, so scripts that write words with combining marks are cut at the marks

commits.subject: 🔒 Drop any stored commit that HEAD has but this workstream doesn't name

why: a stored entry can come from another clone, so a card on a hash HEAD can vouch for, but that doesn't name the workstream, was a forged card that survived snapshots
constraint: a stored commit absent from HEAD, such as one from a deleted branch, still keeps its card

commits.subject: 🔒 Frame commit records with NUL so commit text can't forge them

why: commit text could forge records, so memory could store a commit that doesn't exist and parseCommit could throw on a piece with no subject
constraint: a stored card is kept only for hashes HEAD lacks, such as a deleted branch; the sync merge still joins cards
gotcha: a stored hash on HEAD that no commit there names for the workstream is still kept, since only commits naming it are compared

commits.subject: 🐛 Stop a pushed tip or a forged entry from erasing memory

why: origin's tip is written by other people, and a sync that trusted it could empty a clone, undo a purge, or tell someone to force-push for a false reason. Entries can also hold cards from unpushed branches, so a release must not publish them without an opt-in.
constraint: only a tombstone may remove an entry from memory.
gotcha: when a descendant brings a purged entry back, its tip can't be a parent even though it's ahead, so that sync keeps local and needs a force-push like any other purge.

commits.subject: ✨ Share project memory between clones

why: memory has to outlive a deleted branch and reach a fresh clone, or the reasons behind the code stay on one machine.
constraint: init must not set remote.origin.push, and the fetch refspec must be a wildcard, or plain git push, fetch and pull break.
gotcha: a merge parent that still holds purged text makes it reachable again and pushes it, so a tombstone side is the only parent, and when each side purged what the other holds the merge has none.
followUp: nothing forces a push; after a purge the user runs the force-push sync prints.

commits.subject: 🐛 Keep odd commit dates from poisoning a memory entry

why: a commit from a peer's clock or tools could silently destroy a workstream's memory while ws ship still exited 0
constraint: git limits neither the year nor the offset in %aI, so commit dates are checked for shape and only updatedAt must be a real time
gotcha: a separator byte in a commit splits or shifts readCommits' records, so fields can hold other text and later fields can be undefined
followUp: a commit body can still forge a whole record with a hash-shaped first field; fixing that means changing readCommits' format

commits.subject: ✨ Keep workstream summaries in refs/chamoji/memory

why: reasoning has to outlive the branch it was written on, and a git ref travels with the repo on any host
constraint: writes go through plumbing only, so HEAD, the index and the work tree are never touched
the ref is fetched from other people, so readTree drops anything off the layout and every entry is rebuilt field by field
gotcha: the environment and author.email outrank user.email, so the fixed identity is also set in the environment or a real address would reach the ref
ls-tree answers relative to cwd without --full-tree
followUp: memory sync must not keep a purged history as a merge parent, or the purge is undone

commits.subject: ✨ Add chamoji why to explain a line

why: the milestone exists to answer "why is this line here", and a line's intent lives on the commit that wrote it, so `why <file:line>` blames the line and prints that commit's card
constraint: blames the working copy, not HEAD, so line numbers match the editor and an edited line is reported as uncommitted instead of being blamed on an older commit
gotcha: the commit is read as `<hash>^!`, because readCommits takes one revision argument and a bare `-1 <hash>` would be a single bad argument; it also works for a root commit
followUp: a range such as file:10-20 would need one card per distinct commit

commits.subject: 🐛 Read wrapped intent values and survive odd trailer keys

why: a wrapped Why: line was cut to its first line, and a trailer named constructor or toString crashed the whole changelog through an inherited property lookup.
gotcha: git can hand back a trailer cut at its first line while the body has the whole value, so a value that only starts a longer one is dropped.

commits.subject: ✨ Read intent cards from commit messages

why: project memory needs a commit's reasons as data. Every later task reads the card, so parsing it once at the base keeps them from each scanning message bodies on their own.
constraint: cards stay out of rendered changelogs, so the Markdown and HTML output is unchanged.
gotcha: GitHub's squash message puts the lines mid-body where git's trailer parser skips them, so the body is scanned after the trailers.

commits.subject: 📝 Plan milestone 7, Project memory

why: the roadmap makes this milestone the dogfooding for workstreams, so the plan is the first stamped commit.
